title: Identification of microplastics in wastewater after cascade filtration using Pyrolysis-GC–MS
author: Funck, Yildirim, et al.
materials: The Py-GC–MS system consisted of a Pyrola 2000 (Pyrol AB; Lund, Sweden) which was provided by Axel Semrau GmbH & Co.KG (Sprockhövel, Germany) and a Thermo Fisher Scientific ISQ GC–MS system (Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc.; Waltham, USA). An OPTIMA 1 MS column (MACHEREY-NAGEL GmbH & CO. KG; Düren, Germany) was installed with ID of 0.25 mm, film thickness of 0.25 μm and length of 30 m. The pyrolysis was online coupled with the split/splitless (SSL) injector of the GC–MS system.

Calibration samples with a mixture of PS (BS-Partikel GmbH; Mainz, Deutschland) with a d50-value of 504 nm and PE (d50 of 25 μm) were prepared. The concentrations are shown in SI. Table 4. The respective polymer weights were dispersed in 10 mL ethanol. An ultrasonic finger BANDELIN SONOPLUS HD 2000 (BANDELIN electronic GmbH & Co. KG; Berlin, Germany) was used for 15 min to disperse the polymer particle in ethanol. 2 μL of the internal standard styrene-d8 with 98 % purity (Sigma-Aldrich Chemie GmbH; Taufkirchen, Germany) were added to each dispersion. 5 μL of each calibration dispersion were directly applied to the pyrolysis filament. The results of calibration no.1 (s. Table SI 1) were used to calculate the limit of detection (LOD) and limit of quantification (LOQ) using the signal to noise ratio (S/N) of 3 and 10, respectively. The repeatability of the method was tested by measuring the calibration no. 3 three times over the course of three days.

Blank measurements were conducted. Lab air blanks were analyzed by opening and closing the pyrolysis chamber. Furthermore, the used ethanol was analyzed. To avoid carry over the pyrolysis filament and glass cell were cleansed by a blowtorch after each measurement. This procedure was conducted with the capillary inserted to the SSL-injector with helium flowing through preventing the capillary from melting.

For analysis Thermo Excalibur 2.1 0.114 acquisition software was used. The raw data file was converted by the inbuilt file converter into a cdf. file. Thereafter the cdf. file was converted into a d. file and evaluated with Agilent´s Masshunter 10 qualitative analysis software Version 10.0.10305.0, which allows data evaluation on Windows 10 systems.

steps.title: Set up Pyrolysis‑GC‑MS system
steps.instruction: Install the Pyrola 2000 pyrolyzer (Axel Semrau GmbH & Co.KG) coupled online to the Thermo Fisher Scientific ISQ GC‑MS; mount an OPTIMA 1 MS column (0.25 mm ID, 0.25 µm film, 30 m length, Macherey‑Nagel) and connect the split/splitless (SSL) injector to the GC‑MS.

steps.title: Prepare filament and chamber
steps.instruction: Insert the platinum filament (20 mm × 5 mm) into the heatable pyrolysis chamber equipped with a withdrawable glass cell; verify the filament can reach 550 °C–1300 °C within 8 ms.

steps.title: Program temperature and flow conditions
steps.instruction: Set pyrolysis temperature to 600 °C with a 2 s hold; chamber temperature to 200 °C. Set SSL‑injector temperature to 280 °C, split ratio 1:10, split flow 10 mL min⁻¹, column He flow 1 mL min⁻¹ (99.999 mol % purity, Air Liquide). Program GC: start 40 °C, hold 4 min; ramp 5 °C min⁻¹ to 200 °C; then ramp 10 °C min⁻¹ to 300 °C. Set detector transfer line to 280 °C, electron‑ionization source to 250 °C, 70 eV. Acquire in full‑scan mode, m/z 40–450, scan time 0.204 s.

steps.title: Prepare calibration dispersions
steps.instruction: Weigh polymer amounts of polystyrene (PS, d₅₀ = 504 nm, BS‑Partikel GmbH) and polyethylene (PE, d₅₀ = 25 µm) as listed in SI Table 4; disperse each in 10 mL ethanol using a BANDELIN SONOPLUS HD 2000 ultrasonic bath for 15 min. Add 2 µL styrene‑d₈ (98 % purity, Sigma‑Aldrich) internal standard to each dispersion. Pipette 5 µL of each calibration dispersion onto the pyrolysis filament.

substeps.instruction: Measure calibration sample no. 3 three times on separate days to assess repeatability.
Use calibration sample no. 1 to calculate LOD and LOQ (S/N = 3 and 10).

steps.title: Prepare wastewater samples
steps.instruction: Grind the WWTP sample with a mortar and pestle; take an aliquot with tweezers and a spatula as described in Table 3. Weigh the aliquot in a 70 µL ceramic crucible (Mettler Toledo, Gießen) on a ME5‑F filter scale (Sartorius, Göttingen). Apply the sample to the filament and add 5 µL ethanol containing the same internal‑standard concentration as used for calibrations.

steps.title: Apply solid and dispersed samples
steps.instruction: For solid samples, place material on the filament with two micro‑spatula and fix with 5 µL pure ethanol. For dispersed samples, deposit using an Exmire 10 µL syringe with blunt tip (ITO CORPORATION, Shizuoka).

steps.title: Flush chamber and run analysis
steps.instruction: Before each pyrolysis, flush the chamber with helium for 10 s to avoid oxidative conditions. Run the injection; total analysis time per sample is one hour.

steps.title: Perform blanks and clean filament
steps.instruction: Conduct lab‑air blanks by opening and closing the pyrolysis chamber and analyze an ethanol blank. After each measurement, cleanse the pyrolysis filament and glass cell with a blowtorch while the capillary remains inserted in the SSL‑injector with helium flow to prevent melting.

steps.title: Acquire and process data
steps.instruction: Use Thermo Excalibur 2.1.0.114 acquisition software to collect data. Convert the raw file to .cdf with the built‑in converter, then to a .d file, and evaluate spectra with Agilent MassHunter 10 qualitative analysis software (Version 10.0.10305.0) on a Windows 10 system.
